Revised, literature-informed assessment: The statement’s near-term outlook is clearly negative (“weigh on economic activity … and pose risks”), but the policy stance is aggressively supportive. Cutting the policy rate to the effective lower bound, launching large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanding repos, and easing the discount window and swap lines directly target credit-market functioning. This aligns with the credit/financial accelerator literature, which shows that easing financial frictions lowers the external finance premium and dampens real downturns (e.g., Oliner and Rudebusch, 1996a; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994; Gertler and Gilchrist, 1994). With market-based inflation compensation falling and inflation below target, the deflation risk and associated welfare costs (Dotsey; Ireland; Prescott) justify forceful accommodation at the zero lower bound/liquidity trap. Netting these, the tone remains negative but less so than a purely macro-deterioration reading.

Key sentences:
- Negative: “The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook.”
- Mitigating: “The Federal Reserve is prepared to use its full range of tools to support the flow of credit to households and businesses.”
